key_sub: Nernst: E = E° − (0.059/n) log Q at 298 K.
body_html:
How to think about it

A galvanic cell turns chemical energy into electricity: oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode. E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode; a positive value means ΔG° = −nFE° is negative and the reaction is spontaneous. The Nernst equation corrects E for concentrations.

Conductivity κ falls on dilution, but molar conductivity Λm = κ × 1000/C rises; Kohlrausch's law adds ionic contributions at infinite dilution. In electrolysis the mass deposited is m = MIt/(nF), with F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹.

Example

E° = 1.10 V, n = 2. ΔG°?

−2 × 96,500 × 1.10

Answer: −212 kJ mol⁻¹

Example

2 A for 965 s, Cu²⁺. Mass?

63.5 × 1930 ÷ (2 × 96,500)

Answer: 0.635 g

Common mistakes

  • Adding electrode potentials instead of subtracting.
  • Forgetting n in ΔG = −nFE.
  • Using minutes instead of seconds in Q = It.

faq.a: E = E° − (0.059/n) log Q at 298 K; it gives the cell e.m.f. at non-standard concentrations.

faq.q: Why does molar conductivity increase on dilution?
faq.a: Ions are further apart and move more freely, so each mole of electrolyte carries current better.

items.q: What is the relation between E°<sub>cell</sub> and the equilibrium constant?
Which law relates the mass of substance deposited to the charge passed?
A cell is made from the Mg²⁺/Mg (E° = −2.37 V) and Cu²⁺/Cu (E° = 0.34 V) half-cells. Which half-cell is the negative electrode?
items.e: The more negative E° is the negative electrode, where oxidation happens.

items.q: Calculate the standard e.m.f. of a cell made from the Cu²⁺/Cu (E° = 0.34 V) and Br₂/2Br⁻ (E° = 1.09 V) half-cells.
items.e: E°cell = E°(more positive) − E°(more negative) = 1.09 − (0.34) = 0.75 V.

items.q: A cell is made from the 2H⁺/H₂ (E° = 0 V) and Cl₂/2Cl⁻ (E° = 1.36 V) half-cells. Which half-cell is the negative electrode?
items.e: The more negative E° is the negative electrode, where oxidation happens.

items.q: Which electrolyte's Λ°<sub>m</sub> cannot be found by extrapolating to zero concentration?
c: a strong electrolyte such as KCl
a weak electrolyte such as ethanoic acid

items.q: What is corrosion of iron (rusting)?
c: an electrochemical process in which iron is oxidised in the presence of water and oxygen

items.q: What is a fuel cell?
c: a cell that converts the energy of burning a fuel such as H₂ directly into electricity
items.e: Used in the Apollo space programme.

items.q: Calculate the standard e.m.f. of a cell made from the Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ (E° = 0.77 V) and Cl₂/2Cl⁻ (E° = 1.36 V) half-cells.

items.q: What happens to the conductivity (κ) of a solution on dilution?
items.e: There are fewer ions per unit volume.

items.q: In a galvanic cell, where does oxidation occur?
items.e: The anode is negative in a galvanic cell.

items.q: How does galvanising protect iron?
